title: Vietnam draft lottery as IV for military service on earnings

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Instrumental Variables (IV / Two-Stage Least Squares)**

The draft lottery number serves as an instrument for veteran status (military service). The identification strategy relies on the following logic:

- **Relevance**: Men with low draft lottery numbers were more likely to be drafted and thus serve in the military. The lottery number should predict veteran status (first stage).
- **Exclusion Restriction**: The draft lottery number was randomly assigned, so it should affect earnings *only* through its effect on military service, not through any other channel.
- **Independence/Exogeneity**: Because lottery numbers were randomly assigned, they are uncorrelated with unobserved determinants of earnings (ability, motivation, family background, etc.).

OLS estimates of the effect of veteran status on earnings are biased because military service is endogenous — men who serve may differ systematically from those who don't (e.g., in education, health, socioeconomic background). The draft lottery provides quasi-random variation in the probability of service, enabling a Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) interpretation: the causal effect of military service on earnings for "compliers" — men whose service status was determined by their lottery number.

**Note on the data**: The variable `z` appears to be binary (0/1) rather than a continuous lottery number (1–365), suggesting it has been pre-processed into a "low draft number" indicator. The variable `x` appears continuous rather than strictly binary, which may reflect a propensity or probability measure. I will proceed with IV estimation using `z` as the instrument for `x`.

## 2. R Code

```r
# ==============================================================
# Vietnam Draft Lottery IV Analysis
# ==============================================================

# Load required packages
if (!require("AER")) install.packages("AER", repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")
if (!require("lmtest")) install.packages("lmtest", repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")
if (!require("sandwich")) install.packages("sandwich", repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")

library(AER)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load and inspect data
# ----------------------------------------------------------
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s21_data.csv")

cat("=== DATA SUMMARY ===\n")
cat("Dimensions:", nrow(df), "obs x", ncol(df), "vars\n\n")
summary(df)

cat("\n=== Variable distributions ===\n")
cat("z (instrument) — unique values:", length(unique(df$z)), "\n")
cat("z table:\n")
print(table(df$z))
cat("\nx (endogenous) — summary:\n")
print(summary(df$x))
cat("\ny (outcome) — summary:\n")
print(summary(df$y))

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 2. OLS (naive) estimation
# ----------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("OLS: NAIVE REGRESSION (y ~ x + controls)\n")
cat("========================================\n")
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)
ols_robust <- coeftest(ols, vcov = vcovHC(ols, type = "HC1"))
print(ols_robust)

cat("\nOLS coefficient on x:", round(coef(ols)["x"], 4), "\n")

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 3. First Stage: x ~ z + controls
# ----------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("FIRST STAGE: x ~ z + controls\n")
cat("========================================\n")
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)
fs_robust <- coeftest(first_stage, vcov = vcovHC(first_stage, type = "HC1"))
print(fs_robust)

# F-statistic on excluded instrument
fs_ftest <- waldtest(first_stage, . ~ . - z, vcov = vcovHC(first_stage, type = "HC1"))
cat("\nFirst-stage F-statistic on excluded instrument z:\n")
print(fs_ftest)

# Extract the F-stat value
f_stat <- fs_ftest$F[2]
cat("F-statistic:", round(f_stat, 2), "\n")
cat("Rule of thumb: F > 10 indicates instrument is not weak\n")

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Reduced Form: y ~ z + controls
# ----------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("REDUCED FORM: y ~ z + controls\n")
cat("========================================\n")
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = df)
rf_robust <- coeftest(reduced_form, vcov = vcovHC(reduced_form, type = "HC1"))
print(rf_robust)

cat("\nReduced-form coefficient on z:", round(coef(reduced_form)["z"], 4), "\n")

# Wald/IV estimate = reduced form / first stage
wald_est <- coef(reduced_form)["z"] / coef(first_stage)["z"]
cat("Wald (ratio) IV estimate:", round(wald_est, 4), "\n")

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 5. IV / 2SLS Estimation
# ----------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("2SLS IV ESTIMATION: y ~ x + controls | z + controls\n")
cat("========================================\n")
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df)
iv_robust <- coeftest(iv_model, vcov = vcovHC(iv_model, type = "HC1"))
print(iv_robust)

iv_summary <- summary(iv_model, diagnostics = TRUE)
cat("\nIV Diagnostics:\n")
print(iv_summary$diagnostics)

cat("\n--- KEY RESULT ---\n")
cat("2SLS coefficient on x (veteran status):", round(coef(iv_model)["x"], 4), "\n")
cat("Robust SE:", round(iv_robust["x", "Std. Error"], 4), "\n")
cat("Robust t-stat:", round(iv_robust["x", "t value"], 4), "\n")
cat("Robust p-value:", round(iv_robust["x", "Pr(>|t|)"], 4), "\n")

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Robustness Checks
# ----------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("ROBUSTNESS CHECKS\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# 6a. IV without controls (since z is randomly assigned)
cat("\n--- 6a. IV without controls ---\n")
iv_nocontrols <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df)
iv_nocontrols_robust <- coeftest(iv_nocontrols, vcov = vcovHC(iv_nocontrols, type = "HC1"))
print(iv_nocontrols_robust)
cat("IV coef (no controls):", round(coef(iv_nocontrols)["x"], 4), "\n")

# 6b. Balance check: instrument should be uncorrelated with controls
cat("\n--- 6b. Balance check: controls ~ z ---\n")
balance <- lm(controls ~ z, data = df)
balance_robust <- coeftest(balance, vcov = vcovHC(balance, type = "HC1"))
print(balance_robust)
cat("If z is randomly assigned, it should not predict controls.\n")
cat("p-value on z:", round(balance_robust["z", "Pr(>|t|)"], 4), "\n")

# 6c. OLS without controls for comparison
cat("\n--- 6c. OLS without controls ---\n")
ols_nocontrols <- lm(y ~ x, data = df)
print(coeftest(ols_nocontrols, vcov = vcovHC(ols_nocontrols, type = "HC1")))

# 6d. Hausman test (endogeneity test)
cat("\n--- 6d. Durbin-Wu-Hausman endogeneity test ---\n")
# Manual: add first-stage residuals to OLS
df$fs_resid <- residuals(first_stage)
hausman_reg <- lm(y ~ x + controls + fs_resid, data = df)
hausman_test <- coeftest(hausman_reg, vcov = vcovHC(hausman_reg, type = "HC1"))
print(hausman_test)
cat("\nIf coef on fs_resid is significant, x is endogenous and IV is needed.\n")
cat("p-value on first-stage residual:", round(hausman_test["fs_resid", "Pr(>|t|)"], 4), "\n")

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Summary Table
# ----------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n\n========================================\n")
cat("SUMMARY COMPARISON\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10s %10s %10s\n", "Model", "Coef(x)", "SE", "p-value"))
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10s %10s %10s\n", "-----", "-------", "------", "-------"))

ols_r <- coeftest(ols, vcov = vcovHC(ols, type="HC1"))
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f\n", "OLS (with controls)", 
            ols_r["x","Estimate"], ols_r["x","Std. Error"], ols_r["x","Pr(>|t|)"]))

cat(sprintf("%-30s %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f\n", "2SLS IV (with controls)", 
            iv_robust["x","Estimate"], iv_robust["x","Std. Error"], iv_robust["x","Pr(>|t|)"]))

iv_nc_r <- coeftest(iv_nocontrols, vcov = vcovHC(iv_nocontrols, type="HC1"))
cat(sprintf("%-30s %10.4f %10.4f %10.4f\n", "2SLS IV (no controls)", 
            iv_nc_r["x","Estimate"], iv_nc_r["x","Std. Error"], iv_nc_r["x","Pr(>|t|)"]))

cat("\nFirst-stage F-statistic:", round(f_stat, 2), "\n")
cat("========================================\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign and magnitude:**

1. **OLS (naive)**: Likely shows a modest or ambiguous relationship between veteran status and earnings, potentially biased due to selection into military service (e.g., lower-SES men more likely drafted, or veterans benefiting from GI Bill).

2. **First stage**: The binary instrument `z` (low draft number indicator) should positively predict `x` (veteran status/propensity). We expect a **positive and significant** first-stage coefficient with an F-statistic > 10, confirming instrument relevance.

3. **IV/2SLS estimate**: Based on the historical literature (Angrist 1990), we expect a **negative** coefficient on veteran status — military service **reduced** long-run civilian earnings by roughly **10–15%** (in log points). The IV estimate is typically more negative than OLS because OLS suffers from upward bias (positive selection or offsetting GI Bill benefits masking the earnings penalty).

4. **Robustness**: 
   - The balance check should show `z` is uncorrelated with controls (validating random assignment).
   - Results with and without controls should be similar (since the instrument is randomly assigned).
   - The Hausman test may indicate endogeneity of `x`, justifying IV over OLS.

5. **Precision**: With n=500, the IV estimates will be less precise than OLS (larger standard errors), which is typical. Statistical significance depends on instrument strength and effect size.

The LATE interpretation is that this estimates the effect for **compliers** — men who served because they had low lottery numbers and would not have served otherwise.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: IV/2SLS — instrument: draft lottery number; LATE for compliers (drafted but wouldn't have volunteered)
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Military service reduces earnings for complier veterans
